knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The customer request, the insurer authorisation and the safety clearance are separate documents. Work does not start until the outstanding ones are on file.
Appearance, odour and an owner's statement cannot prove biological safety. Contamination is classified by a competent person.
Water can undermine a floor that looks sound. Visual inspection is not structural clearance, so the area is excluded and assessed.
Water-exposed systems can remain hazardous when apparently off. They are not energised without licensed clearance.
A single moisture reading depends on instrument, material and reference conditions. It cannot prove drying or occupancy alone.
Capacity is not a selection criterion. Equipment is chosen for contamination suitability, location, supply and trained operators.
A wipe-down is not evidence of restoration for porous items. They are quarantined and referred to an authorised, competent assessment.
Early covering traps moisture and hides damage. Drying is a measured trend confirmed before reinstatement.
Concealed damage and possible microbial growth go to specialist investigation. Suspect material is not disturbed to test a hypothesis.
Flood debris can include regulated substances and chemical containers. Hazardous streams are separated and routed only lawfully.
Cleaning, drying, hygienic release and occupancy are separate claims with different responsible professionals. None is certified by cleaning alone.
A possible exposure stops the work and starts the employer's procedure. Self-treatment without a record is not acceptable.

practicalCriteria: Separates a customer request, an insurer authorisation and a safety clearance in a simulated file, and names the outstanding documents before any scope is set.
Records a contamination uncertainty log for a simulated floodwater case without assigning a category from odour or colour.
Excludes a simulated undermined area, records the exclusion zones and evacuation paths, and writes the structural referral.
Completes a utility verification checklist that refuses energisation of a water-exposed system without licensed clearance.
Writes a handover that separates cleaning completion, drying verification, hygienic release and occupancy clearance, and refers each claim.
passRule: Competent only if all five observable tasks are demonstrated correctly in supervised paper or training-only simulation with no critical safety failure. Critical failures include entering an uncleared structure, energising a water-affected system, classifying contamination without competent assessment, sending hazardous waste to ordinary collection, or claiming dryness, hygiene or occupancy clearance. A written quiz pass is not practical competence. Not approved for use until specialist, legal and jurisdiction review is complete.
evidenceRequired: Scope sheet with the outstanding document list for each simulated case.
Exclusion zone, evacuation path and structural referral record.
Limited handover that separates the four claims, from the simulated job file.
Assessor observation record signed by an organisation-authorised competent assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Any entry without written permission or safety clearance, or into an uncleared structural or confined area.
Any energisation, isolation or reconnection of a water-affected electrical, gas or solar system.
Any contamination classification made from appearance or odour.
Any exposure without suitable controls or hygiene facilities.
Any moisture claim based on a single unrecorded reading.
Any disposal of hazardous streams by a route the job does not approve.
Any statement that the property is dry, hygienic, structurally sound or safe to occupy.
